3.text: the merchants who undertake every year to carry the salt allowance from

4.text: Yakutsk to the Kolyma prefer to carry one tenth of the quantity agreed

5.text: upon; for the other nine tenths they get the receipts from the chief officer

6.text: at Sredne-Kolymsk. The salt of the previous years remains in the storehouse,

7.text: and only a small quantity is sold to the people. The large profit is divided

8.text: among the merchant contractors and the officials interested in the transaction.

9.text: It is needless to mention that all the state provisions in the care of such

10.text: keepers are subject to constant reduction and destruction by mice, wind,

11.text: inundation, moisture, mildew, fire, partly real, partly fictitious, for the benefit

12.text: of the supervisors. I found in official reports paragraphs in which even sheet-

13.text: lead is mentioned as subject to desiccation.

14.text: I will give still another example. In all clans and communities of natives

15.text: and creoles, besides the ordinary tribute and taxes, there is collected also

16.text: the so-called “dark collection” (темный сборъ), which is spent without any account

17.text: being kept of it. It goes to all the officials, from the lowest clerk up to

18.text: the chief of the district. I know also of cases where the chief of the district

19.text: would lose at card-playing the whole amount of the taxes of some community,

20.text: and then would make the accounts so complicated that they had to pay it

21.text: again the next year as arrears.

22.text: Strange Reforms. — When administrators of this kind undertake certain

23.text: reforms, still worse things than extortion result. Thus the chief officer of the

24.text: Kolyma, in the year 1888, suddenly conceived the idea that he would

25.text: introduce into his district the smoking of herrings. It must be borne in mind,

26.text: first of all, that there are no herring in the Kolyma River; but there is a

27.text: small fish there, Coregonus albula, the meat of which is soft and very tender,

28.text: which goes under the name of herring. The places for smoke-drying were

29.text: selected, as if purposely, up the river, where even this species of Coregonus

30.text: is quite scarce. The inhabitants built the sheds and undertook the smoke-

31.text: drying. Of course they knew just as little about it as did the official instigator

32.text: of the experiment. As may have been expected, the result was that some

33.text: of the “herring” were charred to coals, others dropped off from the rods, and

34.text: some of the remaining ones were quite bitter and unfit for eating. It should

35.text: not be forgotten that the people on the Kolyma River live on fish as their

36.text: staple food, without bread or vegetables. Only freshly caught or frozen fish

37.text: is suitable for such a diet. Fish dried in the sun and slightly smoked after-

38.text: wards, as is done by the inhabitants, and fish slightly salted (three pounds

39.text: of salt to a hundred pounds of fish, the proportions used among the Russian

40.text: creoles of the Kolyma in salting), are also eaten by them. Strongly salted
